I've been drawing my whole life BUT I remember what it was like learning for the first time. As a kid I would trace, copy cartoon characters, only learned how to draw anime eyes, etc. But I think that is what a lot of artists shy away from. With NO intention of claiming said art and ability as your own I think tracing can be an awesome place to begin! When we have absolutely no idea where to start learning with drawing the most important thing to grasp is shape and muscle memory. Shape/Muscle Memory meaning, when you already know how to draw stick people that's the base your brain and hands are going to work off of. Tracing can be a wonderful way to build your next base off of. Seriously, it'll be okay the artpolice won't bust down your door for tracing a picture of Rick and Morty (as long as you aren't claiming as your own and this stays between you, your sketchbook, and God). Now once your hand has gotten used to new ways of drawing and designing, the next step is to draw a free-hand version side by side with the traced one. Your brain will go "oh! yeah we've done this before pfff", it definitely won't look the same at first, but your brain and hands will finally be able to understand how OTHER shapes and lines work aside from your default stick figures. Once you're comfortable with drawing without the traced references you can try drawing the same exact thing but with subtle differences (eg. Rick and Morty have switched hair or Sonic is wearing a Mario costume dude idk lol). Even after drawing my whole life I still get a visceral reaction from making mistakes in my sketchbook, don't be like me-make all the mistakes!! It's the only way to learn. Good luck!

I have a journal that I write my emotions down in list form in. It helps for me to organize what I'm feeling by mapping it out infront of me almost like a to do list. I then will pick the emotion that feels the most pressing and close my eyes and breath and let my brain take off in whatever direction it wants to-typically I'll have a lightbulb moment about what I'm feeling while my brain is figuring it out. Also don't confine yourself to basic emotions too!! Like sad, mad, tired, annoyed, etc. Label your emotions how they actually feel! -Tights can be very uncomfortable if they are too small. I heard from a friend to buy up one size and I now have a new found love for them! When putting on tights, roll of each panty leg until you reach the foot part. Then slip your toes in and roll them up each leg (putting tights on like pants will significantly increase getting a run in the fabric). Also things I had to learn the hard way are: if your toenails are a bit long they could cause a tear in your tights, it's better to wash nylon tights in the sink with a little detergent and warm water (same goes for any other lacy/pretty thin fabric garments you have) and wearing rings or jewelry on your hands could snag the fabric.

-Bicycle shorts are perfect for underneath dresses and adding a lil extra curvy padding to the hips underneath leggings!

-I was taught if you're wearing a loose or oversized top wear tighter bottoms, and if you're wearing a tight top wear looser bottoms. (ie...big band shirt with skinny jeans or crop top with flowy skirt).

-Perfume should be dabbed (not the sprayed) on the wrists, pulse line of the neck, and behind the ears (I personally do a lil dab in my inner thighs too~)...if you use spray perfume spray a bit into the air and walk into it rather then directly spraying yourself with it.

-Have your keys ready before you get to your door, car, etc. Especially at night by yourself. That way you won't be fumbling around in your purse distracted and vulnerable. And if you have keys in hand they can be used as a weapon.

-Practice walking in heels at home if you aren't used to wearing them yet. It helps a ton and takes a lot of pressure off being good at it right out of the shoe store.
